BMI, Body mass index.
Standards classify a BMI of less than 18.5 for an adult as 
underweight, a BMI between 25 and 29 as overweight, and a 
BMI greater than 30 as obese. A healthy BMI for adults is con-
sidered between 18.5 and 24.9 (CDC, 2014). Although a strong 
correlation exists between total body fat and BMI, individual 
variations must be recognized before making conclusions re-
garding appropriate body fatness (Mueller, 2012).
Differences in race, sex, and age must be considered when 
evaluating the BMI. BMI values tend to increase with age, yet 
the relationship between BMI and mortality appears to be 
0U-shaped in adults aged 65 and older. The risk of mortality 
increased in older adults with a BMI of less than 23 (Winter, 
2014; see Chapter 20).
